style: Warm terminal documentary. A graphite instrument-panel composition with paper-white Menlo labels, thin operational rules, explicit state chips, and restrained amber emphasis on the central brain. Use green only for the routine review path and muted terracotta only for the single critical escalation. No gradients, glass, neon, purple, floating objects, robot imagery, decorative card grids, or generic AI-network motifs.

customize.reuse: Keep the flowchart block's inline SVG connector and node structure, then replace its generic nodes with the SPUR operator, brain, work-mode, specialist, evidence, and human-review labels.
customize.palette: Use only the frame.md tokens. Amber belongs to the brain and outbound work modes, green to routine approval, and terracotta to the single critical branch.
customize.hand_authored_gap: The block supplies geometry and connectors. Hand-author the evidence counter, moving evidence tokens, and the risk-gated routine-versus-critical state change because no catalog block couples those operational states.

layout.header: Top 96px: SPUR / CONTROL FLOW at left, 00:08 / REVIEW ROUTE at right, with a full-width hairline rule.
layout.operator_zone: x=80..300, y=430..650: compact YOU prompt terminal aligned to the incoming route.
layout.brain_zone: x=420..860, y=310..770: dominant BRAIN terminal, evidence counter, review state, and amber bloom.
layout.worker_zone: x=960..1440, y=230..850: three stacked lanes. Each lane contains a mode chip, specialist row, state chip, and evidence token.
layout.human_zone: x=1540..1840, y=390..690: intentionally small HUMAN REVIEW terminal reached by exactly one critical branch.
layout.footer: Bottom 126px: the two-line proof statement and small SPUR CONTROL FLOW label. No persistent copy before the resolve beat.

motion_rules.use: Draw the operator-to-brain route, three outbound delegation lanes, short green approval rule, and the one terracotta critical branch. Measure every inline SVG path with getTotalLength().
The three specialist rows expand from the brain toward authored final slots. The brain stays fixed as the load-bearing anchor; use x/y transforms and out easing.
Bind the returning evidence tokens, the 0/3 to 3/3 evidence readout, and worker RUNNING to DONE states to the same threshold state array so causal state changes cannot drift.
One restrained amber bloom behind the brain lands with the brain terminal and remains under 0.30 opacity; use a bounded hold with no loop.

shot_brief: The viewer watches one operational route become the whole SPUR model: a user prompt reaches the central brain, the brain opens three explicitly labeled lanes for Plan, Loop, and Ad hoc work, specialist terminal rows execute, and compact evidence tokens reverse direction back to the brain. The brain clears routine work in green; only one exceptional terracotta branch continues to the small human review terminal at far right. The dominant motion idea is a route that draws outward for delegation, then reverses inward for evidence, ending on a quiet held proof frame rather than a flashy logo sting.

scenes.motion: On the graphite canvas, reveal a sparse terminal header and baseline rules first. At frame 10, type a compact user prompt at the left edge and draw one thin paper-white SVG route into the central BRAIN terminal. The brain border resolves in amber with one restrained 1.03 scale pulse and a soft, flat bloom. Keep the prompt and BRAIN label readable from 0.45 seconds onward; do not move the camera.

The brain remains the load-bearing anchor. From its right edge, draw three horizontal SVG lanes with 0.12-second staggering. Each lane receives a compact amber mode chip labeled PLAN, LOOP, or AD HOC, then terminates in a real terminal row labeled CODE, VERIFY, or ANALYZE with a small RUNNING state. Rows slide in only 12 pixels and settle without bounce. Use a single amber tracer on each outbound lane to show delegation; no orbiting particles, node constellations, or equal-weight cards.

At 3.6 seconds, create the one pattern interrupt by reversing the lane direction. Replace each RUNNING chip with a compact evidence token: DIFF, TESTS, and TRACE. Those tokens travel back toward the brain on the existing paths while the worker rows settle to DONE. As each token lands, increment the brain evidence counter from 0/3 to 3/3. Then change the brain status line to ROUTINE REVIEW: APPROVED in success green and draw a short green completion rule below it. All other geometry remains fixed.

scenes.text: BRAIN REVIEWS FIRST   HUMAN ONLY WHEN CRITICAL
scenes.motion: Preserve the green routine approval as proof. Introduce one small CRITICAL chip inside the brain, then draw exactly one thin muted-terracotta branch from the brain to a compact HUMAN REVIEW terminal at the far right. Wake that terminal with the label DECISION REQUIRED and two quiet action hints, REVIEW and HOLD; no alarm flash or shake. At 7.25 seconds, resolve the complete diagram into a held frame with the bottom statement BRAIN REVIEWS FIRST / HUMAN ONLY WHEN CRITICAL and a small SPUR CONTROL FLOW label. Hold all positions through 8 seconds.
